Short prerequisite check in author-notes: what material carries hereditary information between generations? Expected: DNA. Support route: school cell/DNA foundations, with reviewed video availability pending.
progression.startsWith: An individual can die while a connected lineage continues; cloning a useful crop creates a conditional shared-risk question.
progression.stopsAfter: Explain inheritance across generations, classify gamete fusion and compare sexual/asexual variation and survival under stated conditions. No detailed mechanism, DNA replication, chromosome division, probability or disease practical.

teaching.task: Explain how reproduction supports continuity across generations and compare sexual and asexual reproduction under stated conditions.
teaching.causalExplanation: Passing on DNA links ancestors and descendants; continuity additionally needs sufficient descendants to reproduce. Cloning usually retains combinations, whereas gamete formation/fertilisation can reshuffle existing alleles. Relevant inherited variation may affect response to a stress; exposure/environment and available alleles limit the prediction.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Connected grower scenario and runner/coral/self-fertilisation contrast. Each caveat has one main teaching home: mutation/environment in asexual; existing-allele reshuffling in sexual; exposure and conditional risk in tradeoff. Misconception diagnoses one shared-risk-to-certainty inference, with concise case feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: Rhetorical crop-risk question, intentionally revisited after inheritance and variation. This is a hook, not a measured retrieval opportunity.
teaching.understandingCheck: Unseen nursery transfer: cuttings from one parent versus crosses among genetically different parents, with some inherited combinations reducing susceptibility. Predict the wider range of inherited susceptibility and explain why reduced susceptibility is not complete survival. Record prompt and feedback separately and assemble an answer-free hold after measured narration.
